title: The Deadly Wave of Molasses That Hit Boston
text:
On January 15, 1919, a storage tank in Boston's North End burst and released about 2.3 million gallons of molasses. A wave estimated up to 25 feet high moved at about 35 mph, killing 21 people and injuring about 150. A court later found the company liable, and stricter building rules followed.

Follow for more history they skipped in school.

Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Molasses_Flood
